messages:
maya: partner flagged tiny per-device rounding that aggregates across fleets (~0.01-0.03 units/hr/device). They see ~2-3% overage monthly on big customers.
aj: can you paste an example event and the billed line?
maya: redacted sample they sent: ```{ account_id: "acct_XXXX", ts: "2026-03-10T15:12:00Z", usage_seconds: 0.48, units: 0.008 }``` partner says invoice shows 0.01 billed for that event.
suresh: sounds like rounding-order + float accumulation. We probably convert to minutes or round per-row before summing.
oliver: marketplace schema expects seconds with up to 6 decimals; partner sends 3. Could be unit/precision mismatch.
aj: I'll run a quick sim: 10k devices, compare interpretations (seconds vs minutes) and integer vs float aggregation.
suresh: short-term mitigation: parse incoming fractional seconds into integer microseconds (seconds * 1e6) and aggregate using integers until final rounding. That should avoid incremental float drift.
emily: partner wants credits if we overbilled. We'll need billing + legal signoff and a backfill plan.
aj: plan: PR today to change parser + unit tests, staging Wed, canary Fri. I'll own PR and backfill script.
maya: also ask partner to send 6-decimal seconds and include explicit "unit_type" in webhook. Add schema validation to reject ambiguous payloads.
suresh: I'll add regression tests (e.g., 0.333333s * rate -> expected total after integer aggregation) and a snapshot comparing old vs new totals.
partner-delta-bot: Created ticket PD-9873: "marketplace usage rounding discrepancy - partner acct_XXXX" assigned to @aj (P2).
maya: acceptance criteria: 1) parser enforces unit_type, 2) internal storage uses integer micro-units, 3) backfill & credit calc script, 4) partner schema update + tests. Also add billing dashboard metric: "monthly rounding drift by partner" to catch regressions.
emily: I'll draft partner comms offering a credit window; include expected timeline.
aj: will post PR link and canary plan in PD-9873 when ready.
maya: thanks everyone :raised_hands:
